assessment: This study makes an important contribution by showing that humans adapt learning rates rationally to environmental volatility yet systematically misattribute noise as volatility, demonstrating approximate rationality with simplified internal models. The evidence is compelling, encompassing a cleverly designed volatility-versus-noise paradigm, innovative lesion-based comparisons between reinforcement-learning and degraded Bayesian Observer Models, and convergent behavioural and pupillometric data. Expanding formal model comparisons (e.g., BIC/AIC) and directly contrasting RL and Bayesian fits to physiological markers would further enhance the work, but these are minor limitations that do not detract from the core findings.
